intro: Round 1 settles the storage shape and the first user-facing workflow. Answer in the page, then copy the block at the bottom back into OpenCode.

questions.title: Where does the bookmark database live?
questions.body:
The tool should work on a laptop without a daemon or an account.

- **A single SQLite file** is easy to back up and query.
- **A folder of JSON files** is friendlier to hand-editing and git.
- **The browser profile** would reuse existing bookmarks but ties the CLI to a browser.

Which trade-off should drive v1?
questions.recommendation: Use a single SQLite file under the XDG data directory. It keeps queries and migrations simple, and a JSON export can be added later.

questions.title: What is the first command a new user runs?
questions.body:
The onboarding path decides what the README teaches first.

- `bookmark add <url>` is explicit and scriptable.
- `bookmark save` reading from the clipboard is faster for interactive use.
- `bookmark import` is the quickest way to bring an existing collection.

Pick one primary path for v1; the others can follow.
questions.recommendation: Make `bookmark add <url>` the primary path. It is predictable, testable, and works in scripts; clipboard convenience can be a later alias.

questions.title: What stays out of v1?
questions.body: Name the feature you are most tempted to build but will postpone. This keeps the first release small.
questions.recommendation: Full-text search and tagging. Start with URL, title, and timestamps; add a search index once the capture flow is solid.
